To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) electrode shorts can be modeled as a stuck-at-1 defect, and (b) the proposed test and diagnosis method is effective in detecting and locating such defects.

(1) Electrode shorts are a common defect in biochips and they are manifested as missing or extra droplets in a bioassay; (2) Electrode-short faults are detectable and can be localized using a simple test procedure that requires only a small number of test droplets and a small number of bioassays.

(i) we have experimentally verified the existence of electrode-short faults in biochips, (ii) we have identified the manifestations of these faults, (iii) we have proposed a testing and diagnosis method to detect these faults, and (iv) we have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method using a real biochip performing real-world multiplexed bio-assays.
